clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock remained at 7:41 p.m. this week, moving only a tenth of a minute backward from 460.8 to 460.7 minutes. This near-zero net shift reflects a week in which executive overreach and civic or judicial resistance nearly matched each other in force.

grand_total_points.note: The net clock movement was negligible, reflecting a week in which executive overreach and institutional or civic resistance nearly offset each other in magnitude.

delta_summary.moral_floor: The moral floor held this week, but only barely, sustained by judicial sanctions against manufactured litigation, a Senate procedural blockade, and rapid civic mobilization rather than by any restraint from the executive itself.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: Week 78's near-zero clock movement should not be read as calm; it reflects an unusually dense accumulation of executive escalation across war powers, immigration enforcement, election legitimacy, and press freedom, matched almost exactly by courts, Congress, and the public pushing back.

traits_moved.note: Twenty-one traits registered movement this week, with all but one shifting toward democratic erosion; only judicial rulings against donor-favoring settlements moved in the positive direction.

long_synopsis: Week 78 measured almost no net movement, but stillness masked intense pressure on both sides. Executive power expanded through resumed Iran strikes, voter-roll purges, press subpoenas, and the firing of a judicially appointed prosecutor within an hour of his swearing-in. Three non-target civilians died in ICE operations within days; a brief safety pause was personally overturned by the president. Trump used a primetime address built on selectively declassified intelligence to relitigate the 2020 election while threatening broadcast licenses, even as CNN, a Republican congressman, and a sitting senator contradicted his claims within hours. Courts delivered mixed results: one judge voided a self-dealing IRS settlement and sanctioned Trump's lawyers, while another dismissed Proud Boys convictions at DOJ's request. Communities organized, a senator was pepper-sprayed, and the moral floor held, barely, through resistance outside the executive's control.
short_synopsis: Fatal ICE shootings, unauthorized war-making, and a primetime bid to relitigate 2020 nearly canceled out judicial pushback and public resistance this week, leaving the Democracy Clock essentially frozen while pressure built beneath its surface.
